elements.quote: A dual review process was used to determine eligibility. Included studies were assessed using quality criteria adapted from prior literature and mapped onto the cancer control continuum.
elements.reason: The abstract describes a review process but never explicitly identifies the report as a 'systematic review'; that label appears only in the title.

elements.quote: System dynamics modeling... is being increasingly applied to cancer prevention and control, but the breadth, characteristics, and quality of these studies is not known. We searched PubMed, Scopus, APA PsycInfo, and eight peer-reviewed journals to identify cancer-related studies that used system dynamics modeling.
elements.reason: The objective is implied through the knowledge gap and search aim, but no explicit statement of the review question or objective is given.

elements.quote: to identify cancer-related studies that used system dynamics modeling. A dual review process was used to determine eligibility.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criterion (cancer-related studies using system dynamics modeling) is stated, but exclusion criteria and other eligibility details (e.g., publication window, language) are not in the abstract.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Scopus, APA PsycInfo, and eight peer-reviewed journals to identify cancer-related studies that used system dynamics modeling.
elements.reason: Information sources are identified, but the date each source was last searched is not reported in the abstract.

elements.quote: Included studies were assessed using quality criteria adapted from prior literature
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the method used to assess study quality (risk of bias proxy).

elements.quote: Characteristics of studies and models were abstracted and qualitatively synthesized.
elements.reason: The abstract states the methods used to abstract and synthesize results.

elements.quote: 32 studies met our inclusion criteria. A mix of simulation and diagramming approaches were used to address diverse topics
elements.reason: Number of included studies and key characteristics (model type, topics, continuum focus) are reported; participant numbers are not applicable/reported for this methods-oriented review.

elements.quote: including chemotherapy treatments (16%), interventions to reduce tobacco or e-cigarettes use (16%), and cancer risk from environmental contamination (13%). Models spanned all focus areas of the cancer control continuum, with treatment (44%), prevention (34%), and detection (31%) being the most common.
elements.reason: The abstract presents main results with quantified proportions for key outcomes/characteristics.

elements.quote: Characteristics of studies and models were abstracted and qualitatively synthesized.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted; the review used qualitative synthesis, so no summary estimate applies.

elements.quote: Diagramming-only studies more often used participatory approaches.
elements.reason: No comparative effect analysis between intervention groups is presented; this is a descriptive methods review without direction-of-effect comparisons.

elements.quote: The quality assessment of studies was low, particularly for simulation approaches... Prior efforts have been hampered by a lack of rigor and transparency regarding model development and testing.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes the key limitation of the included evidence (low quality, lack of rigor and transparency).

elements.quote: System dynamics modeling can illustrate complex interactions and help identify potential interventions across the cancer control continuum... Supportive infrastructure for increasing awareness, accessibility, and further development of best practices of system dynamics for multidisciplinary cancer research is needed.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of results and their implications.
The abstract itself does not state the primary funding source; funding appears only in the funding section of the manuscript, not in the abstract.

elements.quote: The study was not registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) as it was a methods review and did not assess health outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract contains no registration name or number; the manuscript states the review was not registered, and this is not reported in the abstract.

elements.quote: Cancer is a complex, multilevel phenomenon [1-5] in which health outcomes depend on highly interrelated elements across stages of etiology, prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and end-of-life care [6, 7]. Standard bench and clinical research approaches alone are not well suited to account for this complexity... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge (increasing use of system dynamics in public health, calls from NASEM and JNCI) and identifies the key uncertainty/gap: the application of system dynamics to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.

elements.quote: To overcome persistent barriers to providing high-quality, equitable care, approaches are needed to address this complexity and provide guidance for successful intervention... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the need for the review by arguing that systems approaches are needed to address cancer's complexity and that the extent of system dynamics application to cancer prevention and control is unknown.

elements.quote: past reviews in this field have noted a significant increase in their use since the early 2000s, especially in areas focused on chronic or non-communicable diseases [24, 25]. The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction cites prior reviews [24, 25] of system dynamics in public health and implicitly justifies the current review by noting the cancer-specific gap, but does not explicitly frame the current review as an update or replication of a specific previous systematic review.
This is a methods review of system dynamics modeling applications, not a review of intervention effects; no intervention mechanism of action needs to be described.
The review does not evaluate a specific complex intervention or delivery context; it reviews modeling studies broadly, so a logic model of intervention components is not required.

elements.quote: System dynamics modeling... is being increasingly applied to cancer prevention and control, but the breadth, characteristics, and quality of these studies is not known.
elements.reason: The abstract and introduction identify a knowledge gap ('The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.'), but no explicit statement of review objectives or questions (e.g., 'The aim of this review was...') is provided in the retrieved evidence.
This is a methods/characteristics review of system dynamics modeling applications, not a review of intervention effects, so planned PICO comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Included articles: 1) were published in peer-reviewed journals; 2) were written in English; 3) used system dynamics modeling (i.e., causal-loop diagramming, stock-and-flow diagramming, or computational system dynamics modeling); 4) pertained to cancer prevention or control; and 4) were published within the last 10 years.
elements.reason: Eligible designs (system dynamics modeling types) and topic scope (cancer prevention or control) are specified, but settings, populations, and follow-up requirements are not described.

elements.quote: 1) were published in peer-reviewed journals; 2) were written in English; ... and 4) were published within the last 10 years.
elements.reason: Report characteristics are specified: peer-reviewed publication status, English language, and dissemination within the last 10 years.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: most studies included a computational system dynamics simulation model (n = 21; 66%), while the remaining studies (n = 11; 34%) used only diagramming approaches (referred to as diagram-only studies in this review)
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (simulation vs diagram-only; topics; cancer control continuum focus areas) are described in Results, but the Methods do not explicitly specify grouping criteria linked to review objectives/comparisons.

elements.quote: This search period was selected to reflect recent developments and current applications of system dynamics modeling related to cancer.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for the 10-year restriction on publication date; the Limitations also justify excluding non-cancer and pathogenesis-only studies.

elements.quote: Searches for peer-reviewed publications were conducted between February and April 2022 through the PubMed, Scopus, and APA PsycInfo databases
